answer: One knoll cairn backs one identity: it locks a 70-credit bond and raises a lantern etched with a fable pattern. Each epoch it reports its shadow length. An auditor rebuilds the length from the knoll elevation table plus lantern height; a gap over 3 percent, or a serial seen twice, burns the bond. Fees start at 36; the kth lantern pays 36+6(k-1), so lantern 1000 costs 6030; 1000 fakes spend 3,033,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented lantern fails across cairns, since its fable pattern binds one cairn key. An honest cairn costs 36 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
